title: chard cross-configuration matrix
description: A view over many reports, derived from them and keyed on the full configuration tuple rather than on the distribution. The compiler version, the C library, the optimization level and the profile each explain results a distribution column would claim.

chard_schema.description: The major version of this document's shape. When it moves is the CLI contract's rule (`chard --help`; DESIGN.md, "The command-line contract"): a key chard adds is not a change, which is why every object here admits one.

inputs.description: Reports supplied. Cells are fewer only under `--replace-repeated`, where a later report of a configuration replaced an earlier one's cell and `warnings` names each replacement; without it, two reports of one configuration are refused.

axes.description: Every axis and the distinct values observed for it.

invariant_axes.description: Axes with at most one value across the input set. Stated explicitly because they bound what the table supports: a matrix where `arch` is invariant says nothing about other architectures, and a reader should not have to infer that from absence.

arch.description: The report's `toolchain.target.arch`, the architecture every arch-gated decision was taken under; empty where the report carries none. ` (contradicted)` follows it (`x86_64 (contradicted)`) where one of the report's own witnesses of the target disagrees, or an observation is withheld under `target-arch-contradicted` or `target-abi-contradicted`.

machine.description: The machine the run had: what names its CPU (`environment.cpu.arm_parts` joined by `+`, or `<vendor>/<model>`), then `features:` and the sorted `relevant_features`, as `0xc0:0xac3 features:bti,paca,pacg`; `unread` where the report carries no `environment.cpu`. Matched exactly, since one image on two machines of one architecture can answer the runtime checks differently.

execution_basis.description: The report's `environment.execution.mode_evidence.basis`, what established `execution`, or `unpublished` for a report that carries none. An assumed `host` and an asserted one withhold different checks, so they are separate cells.

image.description: The image the measurement ran in: the axis of last resort, distinguishing two specimens that agree on every other axis.

label.description: Built from the varying axes only, so invariant ones are not repeated in every row.

kernel_ownership.description: The report's `environment.kernel.ownership`, whose kernel the cell's run had; `unpublished` where no report of the cell carries it. Not an axis: it follows from `key.execution` and `key.execution_basis`, so every report of a cell that publishes it publishes the same word.

flags.description: flag -> verdict, with the level appended where a graded mechanism has one.

polarity.description: flag -> the report's `observations[].polarity`, for each flag in `flags` whose observation carries one. For a `weaken` flag `off` is the protected state, the flag's effect being absent, so a verdict in `flags` is read with its polarity.

gating.description: flag -> the report's `observations[].gating.rule`, for each flag whose observation carries one; absent where none does. It tells apart the `?` in `flags` that the machine could not answer from one the toolchain's run left unread.

variance.description: Per flag: whether it varied, and which axis accounts for it.

observed_in.description: How many configurations carried this flag. `varies` alone cannot distinguish measured-everywhere-and-identical from measured-once or measured-nowhere, and the note asserted the first for all three.

of_configurations.description: Configurations in the input set, so observed_in has a denominator beside it.

verdicts.description: Each distinct verdict and the configurations that produced it.

explained_by.description: Axes under which every group of observations agrees, as `strength` qualifies them; an axis with an unknown value for a configuration carrying the flag explains nothing. Empty when no single axis fits, the common case once several axes vary.

strength.description: `grouped`: some axis value covers two or more agreeing observations. `controlled`, weaker: no group has two members, but two configurations that read the flag differently differ, with known values, only on that axis and those that change with it by construction. `none`: nothing fits, or an axis fits only with a value per configuration, which `note` names. A value is not known where it is empty (`image` aside), `unread`, `unknown`, `unpublished` or a contradicted architecture.

confounded_with.description: Maps an explaining axis to the axes these inputs cannot separate it from: fewer than two of its values were observed under more than one value of the other. It depends on the input set, and omits the structural refinements (compiler_version within compiler, release within distro).

explained_by_combination.description: A pair of axes holding more agreeing observations in one group than any single axis does, and absent when no pair beats the best single axis. It cannot express an ordered threshold such as a minimum compiler version, so a flag that flips at a version boundary may attribute to any axis correlated with recency.

warnings.description: Sentences a reader needs beside the cells, absent when there are none; among them a mixed dataset's conflicts (under `--allow-mixed`), the dataset's cautions, a set of one configuration, and under `--replace-repeated` one per replaced cell, naming both reports and what the replacement moved.
